chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman from whom her husband is absent for four years, and he did not spend upon her, and it is not known whether he is alive or dead. Is his guardian compelled to divorce her? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. And if there is no guardian for him, the ruler divorces her.
I said: If the guardian says, 'I shall spend upon her,' He (peace be upon him) said: So he is not compelled to divorce her.

I said: What is your view if she says, 'I want what the women want, and I am not patient, and will not sit as I am'? He (peace be upon him) said: That is not for her, nor is it honourable, when he spends upon her.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a woman whose husband is missing and not providing financial support?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *khul'* or forced divorce (*ta'lib al-talaq*) in cases of prolonged absence (*ghaybat*) and financial neglect, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the wife's rights when the husband's status is uncertain. The Imam clarifies that while the guardian is compelled to divorce if maintenance is withheld, the wife does not have an automatic right to demand divorce solely for convenience if maintenance is provided, highlighting the balance between financial obligation and marital stability. This ruling underscores the role of the *Sultan* (or judge) as the ultimate authority in resolving marital status when no male guardian is available.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al asbbah Al Kinany,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a woman from whom her husband is absent for four years, and he did not spend upon her, and it is not known whether he is alive or dead. Is it allowed for his guardian upon him divorcing her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and if there does not happen to be a guardian for him, the ruler would divorce her’.
I said, ‘Supposing the guardian were to say, ‘I shall spend upon her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he (the ruler) is not allowed to divorce her’.

I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if she were to say, ‘I want similar to what the women want, and I am not patient, and will not sit just as I am’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not for her, nor is it honourable, when she is being spent upon’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“About the case of a woman whose husband is missing and absent for four years, has not provided her maintenance and it is not known if he is alive or not, if his guardian is compelled to divorce her. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he is compelled to do so. If he does not have any guardian, the authority and al- Sultan divorces her.’
I then asked what happens if the guardian says, ‘I can provide her maintenance?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not then forced to divorce her.’

I then asked what happens if she says, ‘I want what women want, I do not want to wait patiently as I am.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘She does not have such right and it is not honorable to say so when he provides maintenance.’”
